title: Sale dates the new rolls add for buildings behind City deals
question: Do the hand-saved rolls, above all the 2026-27 roll the portal did not have, show any building behind a City purchase, lease or loan changing hands that the earlier record missed?
finding: The nine workbooks agree with the portal on every one of 3,602 parcel-years the two share (value and sale date). They add 25 sale dates on 30 deal parcels that no 2007-2025 portal roll carried, 4 of them dated 2026. 7 are buildings the City rents, 2 are buildings the public bought, and the rest are tax-credit or nonprofit sites.
how: Each of the nine workbooks was read once into a reduced file (scripts/tools/extract_supplied_rolls.py), keeping every parcel. For the 498 parcels behind deals every current sale date on any workbook was compared with the sale dates on the 2007-2025 portal rolls already on disk; a date on no portal roll is listed. The value before is the roll before the sale; the value after is the first roll whose 1 January valuation date follows the sale. Sale dates are published as six digits (YYMMDD) with leading zeros dropped; they were read as dates. The latest City deal is the latest dated Board file or tax-credit record for that parcel before the sale.
limits: The rolls name no owner and give no price, so a sale date says only that a deed was recorded. A transfer between related companies, a partial transfer, a ground lease to a housing partnership or a refinancing that the Assessor treats as a change in ownership all show the same way. The 2026-27 workbook gives a sale date for 9,507 parcels only, mostly 2023 to 2026 sales; earlier workbooks give one for about 145,000. A blank is not an absent sale. The prior-sale-date column is blank in all nine workbooks. The recorded deed and transfer-tax declaration at the Assessor-Recorder would say who sold to whom and for how much. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
